## Narrative

The most strongly enriched pathway in this dataset is **Eicosanoid synthesis** (WikiPathways WP167; FDR ≈ 0, fold-enrichment ≈ 1001), populated by five of the ten differentially-abundant metabolites: arachidonic acid (C00219), leukotriene A4 (C00909), 15-HETE (C04742), 15-deoxy-Δ¹²,¹⁴-PGJ₂ (C14717), and 5-HETE (C04805). The **Selenium micronutrient network** (WikiPathways WP15; FDR ≈ 0) [disputed by verifier] was also returned by RaMP with fold-enrichment ≈ 292 and includes arachidonic acid, leukotriene A4, 15-HETE, 5-HETE, hypochlorite (C19697), and copper (C00070), suggesting a broader oxidative-inflammatory context.

**Key drivers.** Arachidonic acid (C00219) occupies the upstream apex of the eicosanoid cascade. KEGG graph traversal confirms it is connected to leukotriene A4 (C00909) via a two-reaction path through 5-HPETE (C05356), establishing arachidonic acid as the canonical precursor. The detected 5-HETE (C04805) and 15-HETE (C04742) represent the two major lipoxygenase branches, while 15-deoxy-Δ¹²,¹⁴-PGJ₂ (C14717) is a matched member of the same Eicosanoid synthesis pathway. Histamine (C00388), while not part of the eicosanoid core pathway, can synergize with LOX products to amplify vascular permeability and leukocyte recruitment.

**Biological significance.** Coordinated elevation of arachidonic acid alongside multiple downstream eicosanoids is characteristic of activated phospholipase A₂ and intensified cyclooxygenase / lipoxygenase flux — a hallmark of acute or chronic inflammatory stimulation. Hypochlorite and copper dysregulation, captured in the Selenium micronutrient network, suggest metal-dependent redox stress, potentially amplifying oxidative modification of membrane lipids and contributing to the eicosanoid surge.

In summary, the data point to a robust inflammatory eicosanoid response anchored by arachidonic acid, with multi-axis LOX product formation and an accompanying prostaglandin signal.

**Limitations.** The specific role of histamine, the mechanistic link between hypochlorite/copper and eicosanoid overproduction, and the precise functional assignment of 15d-PGJ₂ in this experimental context are not directly evidenced in the current RaMP/KEGG outputs and should be treated as hypotheses requiring further validation.
